name: @kanzo-tech/graph
description: Kanzo graph view — a GraphAr graph attached to the page's DuckDB, read through the page's Mosaic coordinator as one more client, laid out and drawn with cosmos.gl on the GPU. Sibling of @kanzo-tech/ui, not part of it: the admission rules exclude graphs from the generic vocabulary by name.
//peers: All required but two. `@xyflow/react` and `elkjs` are `./diagram`'s, optional, and reached from no other entry: React Flow draws a diagram's nodes and edges as DOM, and ELK lays them out in its own worker. Both are large, and ELK is EPL-2.0 OR GPL-3.0-or-later where everything else here is MIT, so a host that never draws a diagram installs neither (/docs/design/graph, *A diagram is a second view*). The floors are the releases this package is built and tested against: `ariaLabelConfig` and a `fitView` that waits for the nodes it frames are recent in React Flow 12. The rest: cosmos.gl draws and lays out; `@ark-ui/react` is what every part renders through (`ark.*`), a peer for the reason it is `@kanzo-tech/ui`'s — two copies of Ark would be two portals and two focus traps; `lucide-react` is the icon set the parts draw their buttons with, `@kanzo-tech/ui`'s own peer; `@kanzo-tech/mosaic` is the coordinator the graph reads through as a client; `@kanzo-tech/relations` is the reader of the attached graph's catalog and the crossfilter the graph listens to and publishes into. The Mosaic stack itself — mosaic-core, mosaic-sql — is `@kanzo-tech/mosaic`'s peer, declared once there. `tailwind-variants` is a dependency, as it is `ui`'s and `ai`'s: the parts write their appearance as recipes, which is also what puts this package under the guards (`packages/ui/src/guard-corpus.ts`).
//graphar: The graph reads a GraphAr graph `@kanzo-tech/graphar-duckdb`'s `attachGraph` attached under a name — a view per vertex type, `"<c>"."<type>"` with `_graphArVertexIndex`, and per edge type, `"<c>"."<src>_<edge>_<dst>"` with `_graphArSrcIndex` and `_graphArDstIndex`, and the information files as `graphar_vertex_types`, `graphar_edge_types`, `graphar_properties` and `graphar_chunks` — with SQL through the coordinator, in one function, `@kanzo-tech/relations`'s `readJoinGraph`, which the store calls and whose `JoinGraph` is the snapshot's `structure`. It imports nothing of graphar's or fossil's: the contract is the catalog and the chunks' footers, as `@kanzo-tech/graphar-duckdb` (Kanzo-Tech/graphar `2ec7a22`, after #4: counts typed UBIGINT, `graphar_chunks`) writes it — types in the graph document's order, counts, edge types and their ends, each property's primary key and nullability, a `list` property as a `T[]` column, and per vertex chunk the writer's `fossil:stats` in its Parquet `key_value_metadata` beside the row groups' own `Statistics`. Every vertex type is a node type; the global id, `dense_id`, is the reader's arithmetic over the per-type index, each type's `first` its offset.
//gauges: One gauge per published entry, and one per tree-shaken import a consumer meets; `scripts/gauges.mjs` (through `.size-limit.mjs`) is what each measures, and every limit's reason — each raise, dated, with its before and after — is a row on /docs/design, *A gauge per entry, and its raises written here*.
